item.description: arXiv:2606.13881v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that, under constant-coefficient assumptions, the Ivancevic option-pricing nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation admits a Betchov-type hydrodynamic formulation analogous to the one arising in the context of the vortex filament equation. Along with this structural correspondence, known Ivancevic solutions are interpreted in terms of density--velocity variables. As an illustration of the financial interpretation, we compare the normalized one-soliton density with the Black--Scholes risk-neutral density, obtaining an explicit relation between the Ivancevic coefficient ratio and standard market quantities. We further show that the probability current can be reconstructed from the temporal evolution of the density and demonstrate this reconstruction for an interacting two-soliton solution. Together, these results illustrate how the Betchov-type hydrodynamic formulation can be used to describe the evolution and transport of the Ivancevic density, while establishing a coefficient-explicit bridge between nonlinear wave models in mathematical finance and geometric fluid mechanics.
item.dc:creator: Sandeep Kumar

item.title: Polynomial rigidity of strong-field magnetic billiards
item.description: arXiv:2609.18937v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^2$ be a bounded domain whose boundary $\gamma$ is a smooth simple closed curve, and let $r=|B|^{-1}$ be the Larmor radius of a constant magnetic field. Assume $$ 0<r<\frac{r_0(\gamma)}2, $$ where $r_0(\gamma)$ is the maximal embedded tubular radius of $\gamma$. We prove that if the corresponding magnetic billiard admits a nonconstant first integral polynomial in the velocity, then $\gamma$ is a circle and $\Omega$ is a disk. No convexity assumption is imposed. This eliminates the finite set of possible exceptional strong-field values left by the earlier polynomial nonintegrability theory. The proof uses the two highest reflection modes of the polynomial induced on the space of Larmor centers. A boundary index identity shows that the highest coefficient has degree equal to the true Fourier degree and that all of its roots lie inside the table. After complexification and passage to the normalization of the boundary curve, comparison of the two leading modes at infinity excludes simultaneous poles of the coordinate functions and forces all of these roots to coincide. The reflection identity then implies that the boundary has constant distance from their common root and hence is circular.
item.dc:creator: Dipesh Bhandari

item.title: Reconsidering the Vacuum Energy of a Massive Scalar Field in a Spherical Cavity
item.description: arXiv:2609.39540v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We reconsider the vacuum (Casimir) energy of a massive scalar field obeying Dirichlet boundary conditions inside a spherical cavity. Using zeta-function regularization, we carefully recalculate the analytic part of the zeta function via the uniform asymptotic expansion of the modified Bessel functions. We correct a sign error present in an earlier calculation (PR D56 (1997) 4896) that affected the large-mass behavior. The renormalized vacuum energy is shown to vanish for large mass, as required on physical grounds. Numerical results reveal that the energy changes sign several times as a function of the cavity radius.
item.dc:creator: M. Bordag, I. G. Pirozhenko

item.title: Lax equations for relativistic ${\rm GL}(NM,{\mathbb C})$ Gaudin models on elliptic curve
item.description: arXiv:2204.06137v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We describe the most general ${\rm GL}_{NM}$ classical elliptic finite-dimensional integrable system, which Lax matrix has $n$ simple poles on elliptic curve. For $M=1$ it reproduces the classical inhomogeneous spin chain, for $N=1$ it is the Gaudin type (multispin) extension of the spin Ruijsenaars-Schneider model, and for $n=1$ the model of $M$ interacting relativistic ${\rm GL}_N$ tops emerges in some particular case. In this way we present a classification for relativistic Gaudin models on ${\rm GL}$-bundles over elliptic curve. As a by-product we describe the inhomogeneous Ruijsenaars chain. We show that this model can be considered as a particular case of multispin Ruijsenaars-Schneider model when residues of the Lax matrix are of rank one. An explicit parametrization of the classical spin variables through the canonical variables is obtained for this model. Finally, the most general ${\rm GL}_{NM}$ model is also described through $R$-matrices satisfying associative Yang-Baxter equation. This description provides the trigonometric and rational analogues of ${\rm GL}_{NM}$ models.
item.dc:creator: E. Trunina, A. Zotov

item.title: Weak solutions for weak turbulence models in electrostatic plasmas
item.description: arXiv:2304.12430v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The weak turbulence model, also known as the quasilinear theory in plasma physics, has been a cornerstone in modeling resonant particle-wave interactions in plasmas. Stemming from the Vlasov-Poisson/Maxwell system under the weak turbulence assumption, incorporating the random phase approximation and ergodicity, it takes the form of a integro-differential system, which describes the time dynamics of particle distribution and wave spectrum. The interaction between particles and waves can be treated as a stochastic process, whose transition probability bridges the momentum space and the spectral space. To our knowledge, there is no preceding rigorous analytical work for the quasilinear theory addressed in this manuscript. In this paper, we establish the existence of global weak solutions to the one-dimensional electrostatic quasilinear model for nonnegative, smooth, rapidly decaying initial particle distributions and nonnegative, smooth wave spectra compactly supported in a positive wave-number band. The construction uses the resonance condition to reduce the coupled system to a scalar degenerate parabolic equation, together with uniform estimates and strong convergence of the gradients of regularized approximations. When the initial wave spectrum is positive throughout a single band, we further characterize the equilibrium selected by this approximation procedure. The equilibrium uniquely minimizes a quadratic functional over a nonnegative cone and admits a geometric construction through the least concave majorant of a primitive determined by the initial data. The limiting particle distribution is non-increasing on the corresponding resonant interval and forms plateaus wherever the equilibrium auxiliary function is positive. A relative-entropy argument establishes long-time convergence to this equilibrium.
item.dc:creator: Kun Huang, Irene M. Gamba

item.title: From vertex operator superalgebras to graded-local conformal nets and back
item.description: arXiv:2304.14263v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We generalize the Carpi-Kawahigashi-Longo-Weiner correspondence between vertex operator algebras and conformal nets to the case of vertex operator superalgebras and graded-local conformal nets by introducing the notion of strongly graded-local vertex operator superalgebra. Then we apply our machinery to a number of well-known examples including superconformal field theory models. We also prove that all lattice VOSAs are strongly graded-local. Furthermore, we prove strong graded-locality of the super-Moonshine VOSA, whose group of automorphisms preserving the superconformal structure is isomorphic to Conway's largest sporadic simple group, and of the shorter Moonshine VOSA, whose automorphisms group is isomorphic to the direct product of the baby Monster with a cyclic group of order two.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Reviews in Mathematical Physics Vol. 38, No. 08, 2550026 (2026)
item.dc:creator: Sebastiano Carpi, Tiziano Gaudio, Robin Hillier

item.title: A new look at unitarity in quantization commutes with reduction for toric manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2412.17157v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For a symplectic manifold $M$ with the Hamiltonian action of a compact Lie group $G$, we give a new perspective on the problem of unitarity in the quantization commutes with reduction correspondence. We argue that this correspondence leads naturally to the introduction of what we call Fourier polarizations, whose real directions include the Hamiltonian vector fields of all invariant functions of the moment map. For a Fourier polarization, quantization commutes with reduction unitarily. For a general $G$-invariant polarization, $\mathcal{P}$, unitarity in the quantization commutes with reduction correspondence can then be formulated in terms of the existence of a Fourier polarization, $\mathcal{P}_F$, such that the quantizations with respect to $\mathcal{P}$ and to $\mathcal{P}_F$ are unitarily equivalent. We describe this perspective in detail for symplectic toric manifolds, by considering symplectic reductions associated to the action of a subtorus $T^p\subset T^n$. We consider half-form quantization in Fourier (mixed) polarizations $\mathcal{P}_\infty$, whose real directions are generated by(the Hamiltonian vector fields of the)components of the $T^p$ moment map. We show that Fourier mixed polarizations of this type can be obtained by Mabuchi geodesic rays of toric K\"ahler structures, starting at a given initial structure and with velocity given by the norm square of the moment map of the torus subgroup. We lift these geodesic rays to the quantum bundle via generalized coherent state transforms, which define equivariant isomorphisms between quantum Hilbert spaces for the K\"ahler and Fourier polarizations, where the later are obtained at infinite geodesic time. Unitarity in quantization commutes with reduction in these cases then becomes equivalent to the unitarity of these isomorphisms. In general, however, in the toric case, these isomorphisms are not unitary.
item.dc:creator: Jos\'e M. Mour\~ao, Jo\~ao P. Nunes, Augusto Pereira, Dan Wang

item.title: Discrete $N$-particle systems at high temperature through Jack generating functions
item.description: arXiv:2502.13098v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We find necessary and sufficient conditions for the Law of Large Numbers for random discrete $N$-particle systems with the deformation (inverse temperature) parameter $\theta$, as their size $N$ tends to infinity simultaneously with the inverse temperature going to zero. Our conditions are expressed in terms of the Jack generating functions, and our analysis is based on the asymptotics of the action of Cherednik operators obtained via Hecke relations. We apply the general framework to obtain the LLN for a large class of Markov chains of $N$ nonintersecting particles with interaction of log-gas type, and the LLN for the multiplication of Jack polynomials, as the inverse temperature tends to zero. We express the answer in terms of novel one-parameter deformations of cumulants and their description provided by us recovers previous work by Bufetov--Gorin [Geom. Funct. Anal. 25 (2015), no. 3, 763-814] on quantized free cumulants when $\theta=1$, and by Benaych-Georges--Cuenca--Gorin [Comm. Math. Phys. 394 (2022), no. 2, 735-795] after a deformation to continuous space of random matrix eigenvalues. Our methods are robust enough to be applied to the fixed temperature regime, where we recover the LLN of Huang [Adv. Math. 380 (2021), Paper No. 107545, 91].
item.dc:creator: Cesar Cuenca, Maciej Do{\l}\k{e}ga

item.title: The half-space KPZ line ensemble and its scaling limit
item.description: arXiv:2506.07939v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For each $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}, t\ge 1$, we show that there exists a unique $\mathbb{N}$-indexed line ensemble of random continuous curves $\mathbb{R}_{\le 0} \to \mathbb{R}$ with the following properties: (1) The top curve is distributed as the time-$t$ Cole--Hopf solution to the half-space KPZ equation with narrow wedge initial condition and Neumann boundary condition with parameter $\alpha$. (2) The line ensemble satisfies a one-sided resampling invariance property, involving softly non-intersecting Brownian motions with an attractive potential between pairs at the boundary. We call this object the half-space KPZ line ensemble. For $\alpha=\mu t^{-1/3}$ with $\mu \in \mathbb{R}$ fixed (critical regime) and for $\alpha>0$ fixed (supercritical regime), we show that the half-space KPZ line ensemble near the boundary is tight under 1:2:3 KPZ scaling as $t\to\infty$. Moreover, all subsequential limits approximate a parabola and enjoy a one-sided Brownian Gibbs property, described by non-intersecting Brownian motions with pairwise interaction at the boundary. In the supercritical case, one of the main technical contributions of this paper is the first rigorous demonstration of a structure involving pairwise pinned Brownian motions, previously conjectured in [BCD23]. Away from the boundary, we show that the half-space KPZ line ensemble converges to the (full-space) Airy line ensemble under 1:2:3 KPZ scaling as $t\to\infty$. A key ingredient in our arguments, which may be of independent interest, is a novel identity relating the full- and half-space KPZ equations, which may be valuable in deducing various geometric properties of the latter.
item.dc:creator: Sayan Das, Christian Serio

item.title: On extinction and survival of the Bak-Sneppen model on arbitrary graphs
item.description: arXiv:2506.15500v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the stationary distribution of the discrete Bak--Sneppen model on finite connected graphs of bounded degree, generalizing the model introduced in~\cite{BK}. In the small-$p$ regime, a graphical construction and a comparison with high-density one-dependent oriented site percolation yield a bound of order $p\ln(1/p)$ on the stationary probability that a prescribed vertex has fitness one, uniformly over all such graphs. If the graph can be covered by long chains with bounded overlap, we also obtain an exponential upper tail bound for the stationary density of ones. In the complementary regime, a Lyapunov function argument yields an exponential stationary tail for the number of zeros, uniformly over graphs of a given maximal degree, with explicit parameter bounds.
item.dc:creator: Serguei Popov, Stanislav Volkov

item.title: Quantitative Quantum Soundness for Bipartite Compiled Bell Games via the Sequential NPA Hierarchy
item.description: arXiv:2507.17006v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Compiling Bell games under cryptographic assumptions replaces the need for physical separation, allowing nonlocality to be probed with a single untrusted device. While Kalai et al. (STOC'23) showed that this compilation preserves quantum advantages, its quantitative quantum soundness has remained an open problem. We address this gap with two primary contributions. First, we establish the first quantitative quantum soundness bounds for all bipartite compiled Bell games via a newly formalized convergent sequential Navascu\'es-Pironio-Ac\'in (NPA) hierarchy: any polynomial-time prover's score is controlled by a finite-level hierarchy value, and finite-level convergence gives a negligible gap to the commuting quantum value, or to the tensor-product quantum value under flat optimality. Second, we develop the sequential NPA hierarchy as a computational tool of independent interest, establishing its convergence and a stopping criterion based on flatness, and identifying its conic dual as a sparse SOS hierarchy.
item.dc:creator: Igor Klep, Connor Paddock, Marc-Olivier Renou, Simon Schmidt, Lucas Tendick, Xiangling Xu, Yuming Zhao

item.title: Modelling optimal implementation of an arbitrary $N$-qubit quantum gate within the generalized Bloch vectors formalism
item.description: arXiv:2509.18059v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The optimal implementation of quantum gates for closed $N$-qubit systems is one of the key challenges for practical realization of many quantum information processing tasks. In the present article, based on the generalized Bloch vectors formalism [J. Phys. A: Math. Theor. 54, 195301 (2021)] for a finite-dimensional quantum system, we develop a new general model for the optimal implementation of quantum gates, which is formulated in terms of the Bloch vectors for the unitary evolution operator and the system Hamiltonians, drift and control, and has the unified mathematical form, which is standard for the mathematical control theory and applicable for the implementation of an arbitrary $N$-qubit gate within any closed $N$-qubit system, satisfying the controllability conditions. Within the developed optimal model, the cost functional has both the terminal part and also, the integral part with the special scaling, and this allows us to specify the quantum optimal control synthesis via solving the two-point boundary value problem (BVP) for the system of ordinary differential equations (ODEs), which can be explored numerically by any of the known BVP solvers for ODEs. The numerical experiments, conducted for the implementation within the developed optimal model of a variety of $N=1,2,3$ qubit gates, demonstrate the high accuracy of the model-based results.
item.dc:creator: Elena R. Loubenets, Sergey Kuznetsov

item.title: Spectrum of the wave equation with Dirac damping on a compact star graph
item.description: arXiv:2510.09829v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider the wave equation with a distributional Dirac damping and Dirichlet boundary conditions on a compact interval. It is shown that the spectrum of the corresponding wave operator is fully determined by zeroes of an entire function. Consequently, a considerable change of spectral properties is shown for certain critical values of the damping parameter. We also derive a definitive criterion for the Riesz basis property of the root vectors for an arbitrary placement of a complex-valued Dirac damping. Finally, we consider a generalisation of the problem for compact star graphs and provide insight into the essence of the critical damping constant.
item.dc:creator: Mikul\'a\v{s} Ku\v{c}era

item.title: Nonlinear Landau levels in the almost-bosonic anyon gas
item.description: arXiv:2510.14679v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider the quantitative description of a many-particle gas of interacting abelian anyons in the plane, confined in a trapping potential. If the anyons are modeled as bosons with a magnetic flux attachment, and if the total magnetic flux is small compared to the number of particles, then an average-field description becomes appropriate for the low-energy collective state of the gas. Namely, by means of a Hartree-Jastrow ansatz, we derive a two-parameter Chern-Simons-Schr\"odinger energy functional which extends the well-known Gross-Pitaevskii / nonlinear Schr\"odinger density functional theory to the magnetic (anyonic) self-interaction. One parameter determines the total number of self-generated magnetic flux units in the system, and the other the effective strength of spin-orbit self-interaction. This latter interaction can be either attractive/focusing or repulsive/defocusing, and depends both on the intrinsic spin-orbit interaction and the relative length scale of the flux profile of the anyons. Densities and energies of ground and excited states are studied analytically and numerically for a wide range of the parameters and align well with a sequence of exact nonlinear Landau levels describing Jackiw-Pi self-dual solitons. With increasing flux, counter-rotating vortices are formed, enhancing the stability of the gas against collapse. Apart from clarifying the relations between various different anyon models that have appeared in the literature, our analysis sheds new light on the many-anyon spectral problem, and also exemplifies a novel supersymmetry-breaking phenomenon.
item.dc:creator: Alireza Ataei, Ask Ellingsen, Filippa Getzner, Th\'eotime Girardot, Douglas Lundholm, Dinh-Thi Nguyen

item.title: Strict monotonicity of critical points in independent long-range percolation models
item.description: arXiv:2510.26314v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider independent long-range percolation models on locally finite vertex-transitive graphs. Using coupling ideas we prove strict monotonicity of the critical points with respect to local perturbations in the connection function, thereby improving upon previous results obtained via the classical essential enhancement method of Aizenman and Grimmett in several ways. In particular, our approach allows us to work under minimal assumptions, namely shift-invariance and summability of the connection function, and it applies to both undirected and directed bond percolation models.
item.dc:creator: Stein Andreas Bethuelsen, Christian M\"onch

item.title: Multiplicity of bound states for a class of nonlinear Dirac equations on generalized star graphs with potentials
item.description: arXiv:2511.09285v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper we investigate the existence and multiplicity of bound states for a class of nonlinear Dirac equations on a generalized star graph \(\mathcal{G}\): \[ -ic\,\sigma_1\,\partial_xu+mc^2\sigma_3u+V(x)u=f(|u|)u,\qquad x\in\mathcal{G}, \] where \(V:\mathcal{G}\to\mathbb{R}\) is continuous, \(f\in C^1([0,\infty))\), \(m>0\), \(c>0\), and \(\sigma_1,\sigma_3\) are the Pauli matrices. Under suitable monotonicity and growth assumptions on \(f\), a uniform spectral gap and sufficiently long constant-potential intervals on \(k\) terminal edges yield at least \(2^k-1\) bound states, distinct up to a constant phase. The constant potentials on these intervals may differ. The construction uses half-line solutions and a uniform inverse estimate. For potentials tending to a constant at infinity, we prove compactness below the full-line ground level. In the flat-well setting, the solutions localized near individual terminal vertices lie below this level and provide a ground state through the generalized Nehari minimization. In particular, one localized solution is obtained for each minimum component containing a long terminal interval.
item.dc:creator: Guangze Gu, Ziwei Li, Michael Ruzhansky, Zhipeng Yang

item.title: Optimal eigenvalues on a metric graph with densities
item.description: arXiv:2512.20508v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce and study Laplacians on a finite metric graph endowed with generalized densities, that is, measures of finite mass. One important motivation is that this setting provides a common framework for several interesting classes of operators: discrete graph Laplacians, Kirchhoff Laplacians and Dirichlet-to-Neumann operators on graphs. Our main interest lies in spectral optimization with respect to the underlying measure. In contrast to the setting of domains and manifolds, we prove that a minimal $k$-th eigenvalue exists, whereas the corresponding maximization problem has no meaning. We then establish connections between these optimal eigenvalues and the geometry of the metric graph, including a transparent geometric characterization of the first optimal eigenvalue via the resistance metric, and a Weyl law for the higher optimal eigenvalues.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Journal of the London Mathematical Society 144, no. 4, 2026
item.dc:creator: Kiyan Naderi, Noema Nicolussi

item.title: Madelung hydrodynamics of spin-orbit coupling: action principles, currents, and correlations
item.description: arXiv:2601.10698v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We exploit the variational and Hamiltonian structures of quantum hydrodynamics with spin to unfold the correlation and torque mechanisms accompanying spin-orbit coupling (SOC) in electronic motion. Using Hamilton's action principle for the Pauli equation, we isolate SOC-induced quantum forces that act on the orbital Madelung--Bohm trajectories and complement the usual force terms known to appear in quantum hydrodynamics with spin. While the latter spin-hydrodynamic forces relate to the quantum geometric tensor (QGT), SOC-induced orbital forces originate from a particular current operator that contributes prominently to the spin current. This distinction between force terms reveals two fundamentally different mechanisms generating quantum spin-orbit correlations. Leveraging the Hamiltonian structure of the hydrodynamic system, we also elucidate spin transport features such as the correlation-induced quantum torques and the current shift in the spin Hall effect. This Hall shift leads to a new definition of the transport spin current thereby addressing an open question in spintronics. Finally, we illustrate the framework via the Madelung--Rashba equations for planar SOC configurations and propose a particle-based scheme for numerical implementation.
item.dc:creator: Cesare Tronci

item.title: Boundary R\'enyi oscillations in the open XX chain
item.description: arXiv:2604.05356v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For the ground state of the semi-infinite XX chain with Fermi momentum $k_F$, we derive the extracted $2k_F$ contribution to the R\'enyi entropy of its first $\ell$ sites at fixed $\alpha>1$. Its phase $\sin[(2\ell+1)k_F]$ matches the Friedel oscillation at the entangling bond and becomes the even--odd alternation at half filling. An exact Hankel determinant reduction and Riemann--Hilbert analysis give every term $\mathcal{L}^{-(2q-1)/\alpha}$ for positive integers $q$ with $2q-1<\alpha$, where $\mathcal{L}=4\ell\sin k_F$, with an $O(\mathcal{L}^{-1})$ error within this extracted component for $k_F$ away from $0$ and $\pi$. At integer $\alpha=p\ge2$, exact factorization gives a finite sum over all roots with error $O(\mathcal{L}^{-1-1/p})$. We also determine the $2k_F$ terms of $\log Z_\alpha(\phi)$, where $Z_\alpha(\phi)=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_A^\alpha e^{i\phi Q_A})$, $\rho_A$ is the block's reduced density matrix, and $Q_A$ is its fermion number. At fixed nonzero flux $|\phi|<\pi$ with $2q-1\mp\phi/\pi\ne\alpha$, the two exponential terms have different decay powers. Exact factorization sharpens the integer result. These pointwise estimates do not justify projection to fixed charge. The uncharged sequence and the two leading charged terms agree with earlier generalized Fisher--Hartwig predictions. Numerical calculations at $p=4$ test the predicted subleading coefficients without an adjustable normalization.
item.dc:creator: Miguel Tierz

item.title: Algebraic Structure of Finite-Size Bethe Solutions in the Heisenberg Chain
item.description: arXiv:2605.05589v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The spin-$1/2$ Heisenberg antiferromagnetic chain is the canonical example of an integrable quantum many-body model. Despite its exact solvability, explicit finite-size solutions are typically only accessible via numerical evaluation of the Bethe ansatz equations. Here, we analyse the algebraic structure of the exact, symbolic ground states for chains up to twelve sites using the Bethe ansatz. We find that the algebraic degree of the ground state magnon phases and Bethe roots scale with respect to system size at a different rate to the ground-state energy and wavefunction coefficients. The ground-state Bethe roots and energy are found to become Galois unsolvable for ten or more sites, thus demonstrating the lack of a symbolic analytical solution in a quantum integrable model due to algebraic complexity.
item.dc:creator: Oliver R. Bellwood, William J. Munro

item.title: Quantum geometry of connected state manifolds: When diabolic points act as bridges between eigenstate manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2605.28351v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Parametric Hamiltonians often exhibit point-like spectral degeneracies, called diabolic points (DPs) or conical intersections, which can lead to singularities in the Provost-Vallee metric of eigenstate manifolds. We regularise the metric by a transformation to polar coordinates and develop a formalism in which DPs act as bridges between adjacent eigenstate manifolds, glueing them into a single connected state manifold (CSM). We characterise the topology of this structure and extend the local rules for nodal lines governing the Berry phase to global ones. On the CSM, the class of geodesics can be enlarged by those passing through the DPs. They can be stable with respect to their initial direction, and can be shorter than those constrained to a single eigenstate manifold, providing new geodesic shortcuts. Further, the CSM provides a new mechanism for Berry phase computation along paths traversing the DPs.
item.dc:creator: Jan St\v{r}ele\v{c}ek, Jakub Novotn\'y, Pavel Cejnar

item.title: New Exotic Operators in the Spectrum of Wilson Lines in General Representations
item.description: arXiv:2606.07738v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Wilson lines are fundamental probes of gauge theories. We show that, in sufficiently rich representations, they support a large new class of operator insertions. For half-BPS lines in $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM, some have the quantum numbers of the displacement supermultiplet and define natural defect deformations. By relating their beta-functions to chiral ring OPE coefficients, we show that these deformations are marginally irrelevant, meaning the half-BPS line is IR stable for all representations. We connect these deformations to multidimensional RG flows and find evidence for new conformal line defects.
item.dc:creator: Daniele Artico, Carlo Meneghelli, Michele Savi, Rudolfs Treilis

item.title: Decoupling Limit of Quiver Theories and the Angular Spectra of Extreme C-metrics
item.description: arXiv:2607.08747v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate the angular eigenvalue problem of the extreme charged C-metric. Starting from a constrained five-point Fuchsian description of the non-extremal angular equation, we obtain its extreme limit by decoupling a hypermultiplet in the dual four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=2$, $\mathrm{SU(2)}\times \mathrm{SU(2)}$ linear quiver gauge theory. We derive the parameter dictionary and renormalized Matone relations, and connect the physical limit $Q\to M$ to the quiver decoupling by an explicit coordinate transformation. Regular endpoint conditions give an algebraic quantization condition. Eigenvalues obtained from the truncated instanton prepotential are tested against independent angular spectra near extremality and at larger acceleration. The axisymmetric sector recovers the known exact spectrum.
item.dc:creator: Peng Yang, Kilar Zhang

item.title: Quaternionic Quantum q-Oscillator and Unbounded Subnormal Operators
item.description: arXiv:2608.06032v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this note, we observe that the class of unbounded subnormal operators on quaternionic Hilbert spaces is a solution of quaternionic q-oscillator problem whose complex case is addressed by Szefraniec in [27]. We also address the connection of unbounded subnormal operators on quaternionic Hilbert spaces, quaternionic quantum harmonic q-oscillator and quaternionic quantum Economics using model theory of unbounded subnormal operators. Moreover, we study model theory for sub-2-normal operators on quaternionic Hilbert space.
item.dc:creator: T. Prasad, K Krishnan, E. Shine Lal

item.title: Odd-even dichotomy in the waveforms of modified Emden oscillators of arbitrary integer power
item.description: arXiv:2608.09008v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Closed-form waveforms of the modified Emden oscillators $\ddot x+(q+2)kx^q\dot x+k^2x^{2q+1}+\omega^2x=0$ of arbitrary natural power $q$, and of their damped $c$-deformed versions, are obtained through a generalized commutative factorization that reduces them to Bernoulli equations. We show that commutative factorizations of Li\'enard equations are gauge-conjugated forms of the nonlocal linearizing transformation of Chandrasekar, Senthilvelan, Kundu and Lakshmanan, the factorization constant being half the difference of the roots of the associated linear oscillator. These oscillators display an odd--even dichotomy: for odd $q$ they are isochronous, with period $2\pi/\omega$ independent of the amplitude, within an explicitly bounded range of the integration constant, while for even $q$ the oscillations decay algebraically, as $t^{-1/q}$. The dichotomy is confirmed by an elliptic polar representation, in which the phase rotates uniformly for every $q$, and, for even $q$, by the Bendixson--Dulac criterion applied to the divergence of the vector field. We present a dissipative Lagrangian of Lurie--Rayleigh type and, for $q=1$, an autonomous Sundman linearization that yields a rational first integral, a Jacobi last multiplier and a non-dissipative Lagrangian; for every $q$, $\omega^2x^2+(\dot x+kx^{q+1})^2$ is a Darboux polynomial providing a global Jacobi last multiplier. Explicit waveforms and phase portraits are given for $q=1,\dots,4$, with and without damping, and a recent application to magnon dynamics in the magnetic semiconductor CrSBr is discussed.
item.dc:creator: J. de la Cruz, H. C. Rosu

item.title: Langlands Duality and Invariant Differential Operators: the Case SL(2n+1)
item.description: arXiv:2608.13400v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Recently we started building a bridge between two cases of Langlands duality. The latter is one of the most influential topics in mathematical research. It has many different appearances and influential subtopics. Yet there is a topic that until now seems unrelated to the Langlands program. That is the topic of invariant differential operators. That is strange since both items are deeply rooted in Harish-Chandra's representation theory of semisimple Lie groups. We started with the case of the group ~$SL(2n)$. In the present paper we deal with the group $SL(2n+1)$. The two mentioned groups are similar, but their representation theories is rather different.
item.dc:creator: V. K. Dobrev

item.title: A counterexample to Kenig's conjecture for the Laplace double-layer operator
item.description: arXiv:2609.07947v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We disprove Kenig's 1994 spectral-radius conjecture for the double-layer operator in every dimension $d\ge2$. For every $t>1/2$ sufficiently close to $1/2$, we construct a bounded simply connected Lipschitz domain with connected boundary such that the double-layer operator on $L^2$ with respect to the surface measure has $\pm \mathrm{i} t$ in its Fredholm essential spectrum. In particular, the essential spectral radius is greater than $1/2$. In the plane, the boundary may be chosen differentiable everywhere and smooth away from a single point. Our planar construction develops a refinement mechanism that produces unbounded growth of adjoint resolvent solutions with fixed forcing while keeping the graph slopes uniformly bounded. A closed recursion for the density and its image under an auxiliary singular integral reduces the growth estimate to a certified inequality for Hermitian $2\times2$ matrices. The certificate uses continuous estimates, exact rational arithmetic and rigorous interval enclosures. Localisation and rescaled graph insertions then produce a weakly null sequence of normalised approximate eigenvectors for the adjoint double-layer operator on one bounded boundary. A compact intertwining relation on Cartesian products of the planar domain with cubes gives the higher-dimensional examples without changing the spectral parameter.
item.dc:creator: Matthew J. Colbrook, Siavash Sadeghi

item.title: Localization Lengths for Two-Dimensional Random Band Matrices: Stretched-Exponential Lower Bounds
item.description: arXiv:2609.24426v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider $N \times N$ random band matrices $H = (H_{xy})$ with centered complex Gaussian entries, indexed by points $x,y$ on the two-dimensional discrete torus $(\mathbb{Z} / \sqrt{N} \mathbb{Z})^2$. The matrix entries $H_{xy}$ vanish whenever the distance between $x$ and $y$ exceeds a constant multiple of the bandwidth parameter $W$. We prove that, for any fixed $\varepsilon>0$, if $W\geq(\log N)^{2+\varepsilon}$, then all bulk eigenvectors are delocalized with high probability. Equivalently, this yields a lower bound of order $\exp(W^{1/2-\varepsilon})$ on the localization length of two-dimensional random band matrices for arbitrarily small constant $\varepsilon>0$, improving the superpolynomial lower bound $W^C$ for every fixed constant $C>0$ established in arXiv:2503.07606. A key ingredient of our proof is a new strategy that closes the resolvent flow analysis using only loop observables of order at most two, without relying on the higher-order loop hierarchy.
item.dc:creator: Xujie Lai, Fan Yang

item.title: A sharp norm inequality for entanglement-breaking channels
item.description: arXiv:2609.27906v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For a channel $\Phi$ on $M_d$ written in the generalised Bloch parameterisation $r \mapsto Ar+c$, we prove that entanglement breaking implies $\|A\|_*^2 + \frac{d(d-1)}{2}\,|c|^2 \;\le\; (d-1)^2 ,$ where $\|\cdot\|_*$ denotes the nuclear norm. Read on the Choi state of the channel, the inequality is an instance of the covariance-matrix criterion of Gittsovich et al.; what is added here is an elementary proof in Holevo form and a complete description of the equality cases. Apart from the constant channel onto a pure state, which shows that the coefficient $d(d-1)/2$ cannot be increased, equality holds exactly for the measure-and-prepare channels with rank-one effects $\alpha_k|e_k\rangle\langle e_k|$ and pure outputs $|\psi_k\rangle\langle\psi_k|$ whose overlaps are an affine image of those of the measurement directions, $|\langle\psi_j|\psi_k\rangle|^2 = P + (1-P)\,(d|\langle e_j|e_k\rangle|^2 - 1)/(d-1)$ for a common $P = \mathrm{Tr}\,\Phi(\mathbf{1}/d)^2$. These include the completely dephasing channel, the re-preparation channel of every rank-one POVM, a one-parameter family interpolating between dephasing and the constant channel, and non-unital non-projective examples already at $d = 2$. The qubit case reads $\|A\|_*^2+|c|^2\le1$ and extends to full rank a rank-two condition of Ruskai. The proof sharpens Ruskai's bound $\|A\|_*\le1$ by retaining the POVM completeness relation $\sum_k f_k=0$, which her argument discards; this recentres $A$ from a second moment into a cross-covariance, and is the entire content of the improvement.
item.dc:creator: Eran Kopel

item.title: Non-Abelian sheaf quantum LDPC codes: good and magical
item.description: arXiv:2609.30159v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Non-Abelian quantum codes connect quantum error correction, phases of matter, and computational resources. In this work, we develop a general framework for constructing non-Abelian quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes by gauging sheaf codes via cup products and use it to establish code families with constant encoding rate and linear distance, simultaneously achieving optimal asymptotic scaling in both parameters. In particular, we characterize explicit logical representatives of the full gauged code space, and provide a fundamental treatment of non-Abelian code distance in the sense of Knill--Laflamme based on combining expansion with cleaning to establish protection against arbitrary errors. We further construct an almost-good family with entire code spaces exhibiting long-range magic. Moreover, we use linearly addressable cup product to directly generate linearly many encoded magic states from gauging measurements of Clifford operators. These results extend good qLDPC codes beyond the Pauli stabilizer setting, lay the foundation for pursuing the no low-energy trivial magic conjecture and shed light on non-Abelian quantum phases and orders beyond geometric locality.
item.dc:creator: Zimu Li, Fuchuan Wei, Zhengyi Han, Zi-Wen Liu

item.title: On the Cauchy problem for the Tzitz\'{e}ica equation: Soliton resolution conjecture and asymptotic analysis
item.description: arXiv:2609.30858v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove the soliton resolution conjecture for the Tzitz\'eica equation, which is an important integrable model arising in affine differential geometry and characterizing proper affine spheres. Recently, Huang, Wang and Zhu (Math. Ann. \textbf{395}, 18 (2026)) reported the long-time asymptotic result for the Tzitz\'eica equation with purely continuous spectrum. Inspired by their work, we carry out a full asymptotic analysis of the Tzitz\'eica equation. Compared with the previous work, by developing the $\bar{\partial}$-nonlinear steepest descent method, we reveal that the solutions of the Tzitz\'eica equation exhibits three different asymptotic regions depending on $\xi:=x/t$. For the region $\xi\in(-\infty,-1]\cup[1,\infty)$, where there are no stationary phase points, we rigorously prove that the solution satisfies $u(x,t)=O_\xi(t^{-1})$ for $\xi\ge1$ and $u(x,t)=2\pi i+O_\xi(t^{-1})$ for $\xi\le-1$. In the region $\xi\in(-1,1)$, the phase function $\theta(z)$ has two stationary phase points. The corresponding asymptotic approximations can be characterized with an $N$-soliton solution as well as an interaction term between soliton solutions and the dispersion term with a residual error of order $O(t^{-3/4+b_K})$ with $0\le b_K<1/4$. In the transition regions $\{(x,t):1-\varepsilon<|\xi|<1\}$, the corresponding asymptotic approximation can be characterized by the dispersion term with a residual error of order $O(t^{-3/4+b_\varepsilon})$ where $0\le b_\varepsilon<1/4$. Our results provide a rigorous analysis of the long-time asymptotic behavior of solutions of the Tzitz\'eica equation in different regions and confirm the soliton resolution conjecture for the Tzitz\'eica equation.
item.dc:creator: Shou-Fu Tian, Jia-Fu Tong

item.title: A Hopf Algebraic Theory of the Quantum Magnusian
item.description: arXiv:2609.33587v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a Hopf-algebraic theory of graph coefficients arising in the quantum Magnus expansion. At the classical level, the expansion is governed by directed trees, whereas its quantum counterpart involves loop graphs, multiple edges, and several types of edge data. We introduce a contraction Hopf algebra of mixed quivers containing these diagrams and closed under contraction. On this algebra we define a character $e$ from normalized linear-extension data, directed-tadpole factors, and a prescription for undirected edges, and let $\omega$ be its convolution inverse. Our main result is a universal closed formula for the connected function $\omega_c$ on every finite mixed quiver, expressed as a finite sum over ordered set partitions of the vertices. We also construct a weighted vertex-splitting Hopf structure on the unlocalized mixed-quiver algebra, with convolution $\star_V$ and canonical edge-weight character $\zeta_V$, such that $\omega_c=\log_{\star_V}\zeta_V$. Compatibility of the two coproducts and an explicit identity between their characters explain this equality. We further prove that the two-vertex contraction identity, tadpole factorization, vanishing on disconnected graphs, and boundary data uniquely determine $\omega_c$. For acyclic quivers, the formula reduces to a permutation formula with coefficients depending only on descent numbers. We derive this formula independently from the quantum Magnus expansion using operator products and Wick contractions, showing that the physical graph coefficients are governed by the convolution structure of the contraction Hopf algebra. Further consequences include a refined quantum Murua formula and orientation-sum identities related to Tutte and chromatic polynomials.
item.dc:creator: Li Guo, Joon-Hwi Kim, Jung-Wook Kim, Sungsoo Kim, Sangmin Lee, Jian-Rong Li

item.title: The Riemann theta function near soliton limit
item.description: arXiv:2610.05716v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: It has been known that (the square of) Jacobi elliptic function can be expressed by an infinite sum of single solitons of $\sech^2$ shape. In this paper, we show that there exists a similar structure for higher genus cases. It turns out that this is just a consequence of the quasi-periodicity of the Riemann $\theta$-function. More precisely, we show that the second derivative of $\log \theta$ with the \emph{real} Riemann $\theta$-function of genus $g$ near soliton limit can be well approximated by the \emph{sum} of \emph{real} and \emph{regular} $g$-soliton solutions of Hirota-type in $g$-dimensional real space $\R^g$. This leads to a tessellation of $\R^g$, whose tile is an oblique prism divided into $2^g$ sections by hyper-planes of dominant exponents in the theta function. We apply the results to study quasi-periodic solutions to the KdV and KP equations. We construct the quasi-periodic solutions using the Schottky group, which uniformizes the corresponding Riemann surfaces. We also discuss solitons on quasi-periodic background by pinching some of the homological cycles

item.title: Recovering a Riemannian manifold from minimal surface areas
item.description: arXiv:2610.13405v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the recovery of a three-dimensional Riemannian manifold from the areas of minimal surfaces. We show that areas of minimal surfaces determine the metric on manifolds foliated by minimal surfaces, up to boundary-fixing isometry. This resolves the conjecture on boundary rigidity for least-area data in an exterior formulation, even without topological restrictions on the minimal surfaces. We also prove global rigidity for Einstein metrics on compact three-manifolds with boundary, assuming $\(\pi_1(M,\partial M)=0\)$ and a non-trapping condition. The Einstein result includes the

item.title: Example of exponential many collisions of identical hard disks in the plane
item.description: arXiv:2610.14282v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that the maximal number of nonsimultaneous elastic collisions among $n$ identical hard disks moving freely on the plane is at least exponential in $n$.
item.dc:creator: Hongda Qiu

item.title: Finiteness of planar central configurations of five bodies for all positive masses: On Smale's sixth problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.16107v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that for every choice of five positive masses the planar five-body problem has only finitely many central configurations up to rotation, translation and scaling. This answers Smale's sixth problem for five bodies. Albouy and Kaloshin proved the statement for all masses outside a closed algebraic subset of codimension two of the mass space. We keep their classification of singular sequences and combine local boundary analysis with a global argument on an algebraic curve. We exclude Diagrams~1, 2, 4, 6 and~8 for complex germs, Diagram~7 on curves through real configurations, and Diagram~3 on curves with a positive arc. For Diagrams~5 and~9, direct order estimates show that the product $\Delta$ of all squared mutual distances tends to zero. On a hypothetical curve containing a positive arc, a first pole of a four-product therefore gives a zero of $\Delta$. On the completed curve, $\Delta$ must then have a pole elsewhere. The identity $\Delta^4=\prod_{i<j}p_{ij}$ forces a four-product to have a pole there, contradicting the same vanishing conclusion. The computer-assisted inputs concern Diagrams~2, 3 and~6 and use exact algebra, interval arithmetic and ball arithmetic.
item.dc:creator: Zhe Chen, Zhicheng Tong

item.title: Separation of variables for coupled radiative perturbations of Kerr-Newman-de Sitter black holes
item.description: arXiv:2610.20500v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We extend Hintz's separation of variables for radiative gravitational and electromagnetic perturbations from Kerr-Newman to Kerr-Newman-de Sitter black holes. On subextremal backgrounds with nonzero rotation and charge, an explicit algebraic matrix transformation yields coupled two-component radial and angular ordinary differential systems linked by a common separation constant. The transformation is independent of the frequency and azimuthal number and applies to both signs of spin weight. For real frequencies, we establish a complete angular mode decomposition. We also translate regularity at the future black hole outer and cosmological horizons into ingoing and outgoing boundary conditions, respectively, for the separated radial systems. These results show that exact separation of the coupled radiative equations extends beyond asymptotically flat Kerr-Newman spacetime.
item.dc:creator: Daisuke Yoshida

item.title: A Coupled Fluid Naghdi Shell Windkessel Model for Pulmonary Artery Banding: Partitioned Numerical Scheme and Parameter Estimation
item.description: arXiv:2610.20966v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a 3D fluid structure interaction model for blood flow through deformable vessels with localized constrictions, motivated by pulmonary artery banding in neonates with congenital heart disease. The model couples incompressible Navier Stokes equations in an Arbitrary Lagrangian Eulerian framework with a Naghdi shell model for the arterial wall and a three element Windkessel model for downstream circulation. The shell describes a 3D cylindrical vessel wall with variable radius and is defined on a 2D reference domain. Its low regularity formulation retains membrane, bending, and transverse shear deformation while requiring only first derivatives of the reference midsurface, accommodating piecewise smooth geometries with discontinuous surface slopes. We derive the coupled variational formulation and develop a non-iterative partitioned scheme with a Robin-type interface condition incorporating arterial wall inertia. For a linearized fixed domain problem, we establish a discrete energy estimate under suitable assumptions. A unscented Kalman filter estimates proximal and distal resistances and compliance from inlet-pressure observations. Numerical experiments demonstrate consistent pressure wave propagation and wall deformation under spatial and temporal refinement. Comparisons of the standard Naghdi shell and a modified, predominantly radial shell model reveal how structural deformation mechanisms affect wave speed and displacement. An idealized pulmonary artery banding example demonstrates the coupled fluid shell Windkessel model with parameter estimation. The framework enables investigation of the hemodynamic and mechanical effects of localized constrictions and their dependence on downstream vascular properties.
item.dc:creator: Yifan Wang, Josip Tambaca, Suncica Canic

item.title: Memory effects in the homogenization of a viscous fluid containing small elastic particles
item.description: arXiv:2610.23819v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This work deals with a fluid-structure interaction problem involving an incompressible viscous fluid and a periodic array of tiny elastic inclusions in a three-dimensional domain. We focus on a critical regime where the volume fraction of the inclusions tends to zero, but their density and stiffness are scaled so that they still influence the macroscopic behavior. The asymptotic regime depends on the parameter $\gamma=\lim_{\varepsilon\to 0}r_\varepsilon/\varepsilon^3\in [0,+\infty]$, where $\varepsilon$ is the period and $r_\varepsilon$ the inclusion size. For $\gamma=0$ the solid and fluid equations uncouple in the limit. For $\gamma\in (0,+\infty]$, we show that the macroscopic fluid velocity satisfies a Stokes system with memory: the standard Stokes equations are augmented by convolution-in-time terms arising from the elastic vibrations of the inclusions. The existence of the convolution kernels is established for both $\gamma\in(0,+\infty)$ and $\gamma=\infty$ using semigroup theory. For $\gamma=\infty$ the microscopic problem reduces to a purely conservative elastodynamic equation and the kernels can be computed explicitly via spectral decomposition. They are oscillatory and almost-periodic in time, yielding a persistent, non-decaying memory. For $\gamma\in(0,+\infty)$ the microscopic elastodynamic equation is coupled to a local Stokes problem, whose viscous dissipation yields memory kernels that decay to zero at infinity.
item.dc:creator: Juan Casado-D\'iaz, Antonio Rafael Hormigo-Molina
